hypothesis: Using ceil(n/4096) partials capped at 1024 preserves the measured 1024-CTA mapping at the largest size while reducing CTA count for smaller inputs. This may lower overhead there, but could also reduce useful parallelism; the full-call effect requires measurement.
notes: Retains the fused paired-load mapping and dynamic finalizer. Each positive-n CTA writes a current-call partial; the finalizer consumes only active partials and overwrites output. The odd-tail owner is computed modulo the active partial count. No performance improvement is assumed.
transformations: Retain the fused absolute-sum, 128-thread paired-tile mapping, aligned float2 path with scalar fallback, CUB CTA reduction, and one-CTA finalizer.
Set partial_count to ceil(n/4096), capped at 1024, and use that active count for both the pair grid stride and finalizer fan-in.
Assign an odd final element using its tile index modulo the active partial count, with an explicit zero-output path for n<=0.
